blocks.title: Start with a Pod
blocks.what: This is the Pod from the first lesson, named sized-web.
blocks.why: CPU and memory settings belong to each container, so you need a Pod to put them in.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: A Pod, as in the first lesson
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sized-web

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: One container from the nginx image.
blocks.why: Requests and limits are set on each container, inside this list.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without containers, Kubernetes rejects the Pod.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sized-web
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.30.4

blocks.title: What it needs: requests
blocks.what: Requests say how much CPU and memory the container needs. 1000m is one CPU, and Mi means mebibytes.
blocks.why: The scheduler only places the Pod on a node with this much CPU and memory still free.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Pod still runs, but the scheduler cannot plan for it, so busy nodes may get too full.
blocks.comment: The CPU and memory this container needs
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sized-web
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.30.4
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: {{cpu}}
          memory: 64Mi

blocks.title: Its ceiling: limits
blocks.what: Limits are the most the container may use. CPU above the limit is slowed down.
blocks.why: Limits stop one container from starving others. A container that uses more memory than its limit is stopped.
blocks.ifRemoved: The container can use any spare CPU and memory on the node.
blocks.comment: The most CPU and memory this container may use
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sized-web
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.30.4
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: {{cpu}}
          memory: 64Mi
        limits:
          cpu: 500m
          memory: 128Mi

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Pods are in the core v1 API.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Pod runs one or more containers together.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The Pod's name. It must be unique among Pods in the same namespace.
notes.spec: The desired state: what you want Kubernetes to run.
notes.spec.containers: The containers in this Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.containers[].name: The container's name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.containers[].image: The image to run, with a version tag. A fixed tag runs the same version every time.
notes.spec.containers[].resources: CPU and memory settings for this container.
notes.spec.containers[].resources.requests: What the container needs. The scheduler uses these numbers to choose a node.
notes.spec.containers[].resources.requests.cpu: CPU the container needs. 1000m equals one CPU, so 250m is a quarter.
notes.spec.containers[].resources.requests.mem: Memory the container needs. Mi means mebibytes.
notes.spec.containers[].resources.limits: The most the container may use.
notes.spec.containers[].resources.limits.cpu: The CPU ceiling. Above it, the container is slowed down, not stopped.
notes.spec.containers[].resources.limits.memor: The memory ceiling. Above it, the container is stopped and may be restarted.

tryIt.result: The Requests and Limits sections show your values.
Allocated resources shows how much of each node is already requested.
